projects.name: Consumption of ODS reduced (Joint programme HPMP Stage II)
projects.description: Iran`s HPMP was approved in the 63rd Meeting of the Executive Committee. HPMP included investment activities in RAC sector as well as foam sector and project management component. Total funding that was approved was US $10.39 million. Over the last three years, Iran has implemented a range of activities including investment projects, awareness and information outreach activities and regulations for facilitating HCFC phase-out. Agreements were signed with the manufacturing companies covered under HPMP in RAC applications and foam sector including continuous and discontinuous sandwich panels and domestic refrigerators. In addition to the above, the Government has enacted policies and regulations to control growth of HCFC consumption in the manufacturing sector; implemented licensing and quota system to restrict import of HCFCs to limits specified in the agreement, and carried out training program for service technicians and enforcement officials. The above measures have helped the country in constraining the growth of HCFC-22 and HCFC-141b consumption in Iran.
projects.outcome: Capacities in government and private sector enhanced through provision of technical support and technological solutions to reduce carbon emissions

projects.name: Solar-powered infrastructure in vulnerable communities to enhance energy resilience is implemented
projects.description: In 2023, the first phase of the project established two solar power plants: one with a capacity of 192 kWp in Saveh refugee settlement and another with 52 kWp in Torbat-e Jam refugee settlement. The second phase, initiated in June 2024, involves expanding the Torbat-e Jam plant to 200 kWp and installing a new 200 kWp solar power plant in Semnan refugee settlement. The expansion phase in Torbat-e Jam settlement was successfully completed in July 2025, increasing the capacity to 200 kWp. Another solar power plant with a capacity of 200 kWp in Semnan settlement initiated in November 2025 and currently is in the  implementation phase.

projects.name: Efficient sewage management to enhance government capacities on climate change adaptation
projects.description:
Based on a partnership with the provincial Water and wastewater Company, the construction of a comprehensive sewage collection network in Kohak was committed by this company, while UNICEF committed to construct the treatment package. Construction of this Sewage Treatment Plant in Kohak village, in Zahak county of Sistan and Baluchestan province, preserves water resources form contamination, benefiting 10,000 local population in Kohak. In collaboration with the project consulting company, the engineering services were successfully completed, encompassing design, calculations, technical specifications, and necessary documentation across structural, mechanical, electrical, and civil disciplines. These deliverables were handed over to the relevant stakeholders, ensuring alignment with project standards and requirements. The design of the system is such that the quality of the treated wastewater would meet the environmental standards set by the Iranian Department of Environmental for the nutrients, heavy metals and microbiological parameters, allowing its outlet to be used for green space irrigation.

A leading company from the Iranian private sector was selected as the contractor for the construction, transportation, installation, and utilization of the sewage treatment plant. The construction of the plant started in the company’s workshop in Isfahan and was completed by September 2024, including all 6 sewage reservoirs, and the package was ready to be transferred to Kohak. 

Following the initial phases, site preparation in Kohak was carried out, ensuring the area was fully prepared for the installation of the treatment package. The workshop mobilization in Kohak was successfully completed in September 2024, including the installation and commissioning of essential machinery, tools, and materials at the project site. This involved setting up prefabricated rooms, pumps, lights, electric panels, and tachometers to support the construction and operation of the facility.

The construction of a concrete platform for the sewage treatment package was the next stage. The platform was successfully completed in October 2024, and the treatment system was transferred from Isfahan to Kohak and installed over it. The contractor utilized the capacity of local concrete delivery companies to facilitate the construction process.

.Day-to-day resident technical supervision during the execution process was carried out by a qualified consulting company from the private sector, contracted by the provincial WWC. UNICEF, in collaboration with the provincial WWC, also provided high-level technical oversight of the project in coordination with the consulting company.

As a result of this support, the water quality of aquifers (Chahnimes) will be improved, leading to improved water quality for the Niatak Refugee settlement which is supplied through this wate rresource and environmental sanitation in areas will be improved, leading to the advanced well-being of the refugees and the people from the host communities living in this area. This project was completed by the end of December 2024. The commissioning and utilization was followed in 2025. This is the last component of the joint initiative between the Republic of Korea and UNICEF Iran with the current funding.

framework.name: ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION, INTEGRATED NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE
framework.description: The third UNSDCF pillar is devoted to environmental conservation, sustainable use of natural resources, and the capacity to address climate challenges. The environment pillar would promote the integration of environment-friendly policies into all sectors, promote improved management of natural resources and biodiversity conservation, and would work to increase national capacities to address climate action, including through international advocacy for climate finance.

framework.name: DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT
framework.description: In the area of disaster risk reduction and management, the UNSDCF would support programmes that integrate disaster risk reduction into development plans and programmes and strengthen institutional capacities for effective disaster preparedness, response and recovery while enhancing the capacities of people working in the area of disaster resilience, risk reduction and preparedness. The pillar would help integrate disaster risk reduction into development plans and programmes among a wide variety of stakeholders and would work to increase institutional capacities for managing disaster risk reduction, preparedness, response and recovery.

framework.name: DRUG CONTROL
framework.description:
The Cooperation Framework will support improved access to evidence-based drug prevention, treatment, harm reduction, and drug-related services and would help to strengthen national capacity for effective border management and drug trafficking control, including drug-related crime, by providing effective international financial and technological assistance. The United Nations partners would work to increase and improve the available services and would work with the Government to address the issues of border management, illicit trafficking of drugs, and drug-related
crime.

children.name: By 2027, more people of Iran are protected from drug use, and the capacity for effective border management and countering illicit trafficking is enhanced.
children.description: The United Nations System’s support will be provided through a set of two intermediate outcomes that define the strategic thrust of the United Nations offer.
